answer.rationale: Rollback is ruled out by compliance. A circuit breaker targets a failing dependency, which isn't indicated here, and regional failover mid-peak risks in-flight customer writes. The remaining levers are route_read_replicas and add_capacity. Read/write contention on the primary is a common cause of write-path p99 degradation under heavy settlement load, and memory_b5 shows routing report queries to replicas recovered write latency the same day with no risk to writes — it is reversible and non-destructive. I want b5 verified to confirm its effect was on write latency (not just dashboard load) and b3 to confirm whether capacity headroom was the decisive factor in a comparable peak scenario, in case add_capacity is the better fit. Starting with a guarded subset of read traffic rather than a full cutover, since the current degradation may be write-path-internal (e.g., the new release) rather than read contention.
